subject: general
question: Tangent drawn from a point P, touches the circle at Q. O is the centre of this circle. If PQ = 12 cm and OQ = 5 cm, then what is the value of OP?
solution:
Given:

Tangent drawn from a point P, touches the circle at Q.

O is the centre of this circle.

PQ = 12 cm and OQ = 5 cm,

Concept used:

1. The radius and tangent of a circle at a point of contact is always perpendicular to each other. So the angle is 90°.

2. Pythagoras Theorem: Base² + Perpendicular² = Hypotenuse²

Calculation: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3cfec2bb0af910aaaa4ceaa47829ab7d0428a346277be81cfe39bceddc8f5cc1.png] 

According to the concept,

Since ∠OQP is 90°, ΔPQO is a right-angled triangle.

OP is the hypotenuse.

Now, OP

⇒ sqrt {OQ² + PQ²}

⇒ sqrt {5² + 12²}

⇒ sqrt {169} = 13 cm

∴ The value of OP is 13 cm.
